newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Wiesenthal wants Peron Nazi passports investigated.
newsitem.headline: Wiesenthal wants Peron Nazi passports investigated.

text.p: Simon Wiesenthal Centre Nazi hunters said on Monday they want an investigation into allegations that Argentina gave thousands of blank passports to Nazis fleeing Europe at the end of the Second World War.

The centre, dedicated to hunting down Nazi war criminals, has asked Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella to look into declarations made over the weekend by Pedro Bianchi, an attorney for Erich Priebke, the former SS captain extradited from Argentina to Italy for a war crimes trial.

Bianchi was quoted by local media as saying that while he was a Foreign Ministry lawyer during the first presidency of Juan Peron from 1945 to 1947 Argentina gave 2,000 blank passports and 8,000 other identification papers to Nazis on Peron's orders.

"In 1945 the government negotiated the supply of documentation to Germany that allowed the entry of Nazis in the country," Bianchi said at his home in Bariloche, the Andean ski resort that was also Priebke's home for decades.
"Under this scheme only about 2,000 Nazis entered Argentina, many received the identification papers but they settled down in other countries such as Bolivia, Brazil and Paraguay," he said.

Under Peron, an admirer of Italian fascist ruler Benito Mussolini, Argentina became a haven for war criminals such as Hilter's confidante Martin Bormann, Auschwitz doctor Josef Mengele and Holocaust "architect" Adolf Eichmann.

Shimon Samuels, director for Europe and Latin America at the Los Angeles-based Wiesenthal Centre, said in a statement that he had written to Di Tella asking him for "an immediate investigation about Bianchi's declarations about the role of Peron in the entry into Argentina of fleeing Nazis."

Argentina is trying to shake off its image as a haven for Nazi war criminals and has opened up Central Bank archives for Jewish investigators trying to track down gold stolen from Jewish victims of the Holocaust by the Nazis.

A secret U.S. document declassified two months ago, sent from the U.S. Embassy in Buenos Aires in April 1945, estimated the Nazis secretly sent more than $1 billion for investment in Argentina just a month before the Second World War ended.
